Ruling: representation; project retained. Form 8880 (2025), line 7, "If zero, stop; you can’t take this credit"; line 9, "Note: If line 9 is zero, stop; you can’t take this credit"; p. 2, Credit Limit Worksheet, "But if zero or less, stop; you can’t take the credit—don’t file this form"; p. 2, Who Can Take This Credit, "However, you can’t take the credit if either of the following applies". The reply enters the smaller of lines 10 and 11 and lets each stop show as a zero there (line 7 or line 9 zero makes line 10 zero; worksheet line 3 zero makes line 11 zero). The project takes $0 through f8880.can_take, a nested choose that decides the AGI test first (line 8 within the limit, so line 9 is not zero), then the worksheet, then contributions in a column whose person can take the credit, then line 7 (owner decision 2026-11-07, eligibility AGI-first). It gives the same amount on every completed return: above the limit line 9 is 0.0, with no room line 11 is zero, and with no counted contributions line 6 is zero in both columns, so line 7 is zero. The order changes only which questions are asked and, where line 8 refuses, that the refusal of line 8 is reached before contributions are.

Ruling: representation; f8880 p. 2, Line 4: "Enter the total amount of distributions you, and your spouse if filing jointly, received after 2022 and before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)"; "If you're filing a joint return, include both spouses' amounts in both columns". Ruling: representation; project retained. On a joint return both sides add both spouses' person.sav_prior_joint (the project by a sum over the two person entries, the second by one sum per role), so they agree. They differ only on a return that is not joint, where the second adds the taxpayer's person.sav_prior_joint and the project counts nothing for it: the project asks that input for a joint return only (its question begins "On a joint return:") and on any other return puts all of the filer's 2023, 2024 and early-2026 distributions in person.sav_prior_other ("on a return that is not a joint return: all your distributions in 2023 and 2024, and in 2026 before the due date"), which both sides count in column (a). f8880 p. 2, Line 4, "Enter the total amount of distributions you, and your spouse if filing jointly, received after 2022 and before the due date of your 2025 return"; "If you're filing a joint return, include both spouses' amounts in both columns. Exception. Don't include your spouse's distributions with yours ... if you and your spouse didn't file a joint return for the year the distribution was received". The 2026 part follows amb.2025.savers_2026_joint.
